jobs.description:
Phorms Education currently runs five bilingual, German-English nurseries within Heilbronn and the surrounding area as part of a cooperation with the Schwarz Group. Another daycare center will open in Bad Friedrichshall at the beginning of 2026. We care for children between the ages of 0 and 6 years in an open and partially immersive concept. Our facilities offer well-equipped functional rooms and outdoor play areas. The pedagogical focus is on bilingualism, music and STEM - the children always remain at the centre of our needs-oriented work and are involved in the day-to-day life of the nursery.

The company nurseries are part of the Phorms Education SE network of bilingual schools and nurseries, that has been enriching the educational landscape in Germany since 2006.

For our nurseries in Heilbronn/Erlenbach/Weinsberg/Bad Friedrichshall we are looking for a motivated and qualified

Early Childhood Educator

(in part-time or full-time)

Our Benefits

- An attractive salary with additional benefits (e.g. company pension scheme, monthly public transport ticket and free, freshly prepared lunch that changes daily)
- A relocation allowance and all paperwork completed and prepared for residency and work permits
- Continuing professional development opportunities
- Open concept with individual support for each child
- Innovative educational concepts and state of the art educational resources
- Short-term provision of employee housing at current market prices for a relaxed arrival

Your Responsibilities  

- Holistic support of our children in the cognitive, emotional, and creative areas
- Preparation and follow-up as well as implementation of parent meetings
- Regular observation of the holistic development and abilities of kindergarten children

Your Profile

- Certified training as an early childhood educator, a degree in education or comparable education that enables you to work as a specialist or supplementary staff member by the respective local authorities
- Identify with our pedagogical concept and are motivated to creatively implement it collaboratively as a team
- Motivated to co-create new pedagogical methodologies to continuously develop with the organisation
- Interest in working in a bilingual and international atmosphere
- Motivated and committed to working as part of a team
- Fluent English skills and German language skills at least level B2

Interested in re-shaping education? Bring your new ideas to life with us and apply now via our website (https://www.phorms.de/en/career/jobs/job/early-childhood-educator/?utm_source=afa&utm_medium=jobanzweb&utm_campaign=BaW%C3%BC_KiTa_Early_Childhood_Educator_engl_0521) .

Please visit jobs.phorms.de (https://www.phorms.de/en/career/overview/)  for more details and do not hesitate to contact Carolin and Lisa, via careers@phorms.de (https://mailto:careers@phorms.de) .

We look forward to your application!

Job description

Be a Founding Member of our New Connectivity Design Hub in Manching

Help us build the "Manching Footprint" of Connectivity & Comms. We are looking for a Senior Comms Engineer/Architect/Lead who thrives in "Brand New" environments. Based in our new Manching Design Office, you will take the lead on end-to-end development—from first concept to final qualification of all Connectivity Systems such as Tactical Datalinks (as but not only L-16), Comms Managers, IFDL, IVDL, CCAs C2 links for Air Power products such as Fighters, FCAS, CCAs, MuT, A400M…

Why this is different: This is the birth of our "Manching Team." You have the rare chance to bridge two worlds: the deep, established expertise of our Connectivity domain and the fresh, high-stakes opportunities emerging from new programs in Manching. You aren't just joining a legacy; you are scaling it into a new big team full of professional opportunities.

However, for all that, we need a skilful professional with proven knowledge in (some of) Systems Engineering or Connectivity, Tactical DataLinks, Satcom, Architectures definition, ready to be fully empowered and taking ownership of all Integration and Design Activities always paying attention to the future by means of innovation and R&T.

The Reward: A clear development path in a high-visibility, innovative discipline reporting directly to the HO Domain.

Ready for the challenge?

** Your location**

Located about an hour’s drive north of Munich, Manching is an up-and-coming market town that offers a wide range of leisure and cultural activities. Here, you can enjoy the quality of life in the countryside while the pleasures of near-by cities are still within easy reach.

** Our Benefits for You**

- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.
- Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.
- Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.
- Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.
- Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.

Your Tasks and Responsibilities

- Definition and Design of the Connectivity architecture
- Support Customer (German mainly) meetings, Top Level requirements generation
- Alignment with Domain Connectivity Strategy considering National Programs specific requirements
- Suppliers Selection, RFP and RFI generation and analysis together with Procurement
- L1/L2/L3 Requirement definition and validation
- Support interface definition of interfacing systems and equipment
- Ensure requirement traceability and coverage
- Support L2/L3 system test activity

Desired Skills and Qualifications

- Master's degree in Communications/Aerospace-/Software Engineering or comparable studies
- At least 3 years of professional experience
- Experience in Connectivity Systems such as Satcom
- Experience in System Design and Development
- Strong collaboration and interpersonal skills, showing a great team spirit
- Fluent in English and German (C1 Level)

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

About the LSM
The Graduate School Life Science Munich (LSM) is an international doctoral programme at one of Europe's leading research universities - Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU). The programme spans a wide range of disciplines including Biochemistry, Cell and Developmental Biology, Ecology, Genetics, Microbiology, Pharmacology, Plant Sciences, Zoology, and more. Doctoral candidates join a vibrant, diverse, and truly international research community at the LMU Biocenter in Planegg-Martinsried.

Doctoral Positions in Bioinformatics, Botany, Epigenetics, Ecology, Neuroscience, Plant Genetics, Systematic Zoology & more - Graduate School Life Science Munich (LSM), LMU Munich This year, two pathways are available:

1. Independent Research Proposals (new this year)
A number of LSM faculty members are open to receiving original research proposals in specific areas. Rather than applying to a pre-defined project, candidates develop their own original proposal inspired by the research interests of a participating faculty member. Should a proposal be of interest to the potential supervisor, they would be willing to support the candidate in identifying and applying for appropriate funding - such as a fellowship, scholarship, or third-party funding.
Participating faculty members and their research areas:

Prof. Claude Becker - Epigenetics, epigenomics, plant-microbe interactions, biosynthetic gene clusters

Prof. Alexander Keller - Biodiversity, AI and computer vision, plant-pollinator interactions, ecological genomics

Prof. Dario Leister - Regulation and improvement of photosynthesis (open to CSC candidates only)

Prof. Michael Matschiner - Phylogenetics, adaptive radiation, museum and fossil specimens

Dr. Natascha Turetzek - Arthropod evo-devo, gene duplication, sensory organ diversification, thermal stress

For full research area abstracts, please visit: https://www.bio.lmu.de/lsm/en/become-an-lsm-student/recruiting-labs-doctoral-positions/index.html#st_accordion__master_1

1. Doctoral Positions
The following doctoral positions are currently available. Please note that for all positions listed below, funding is still in the process of being secured.
Supervisors are committed to supporting promising candidates in identifying and applying for appropriate funding - such as a fellowship, scholarship, or third-party funding.

Antisense oligonucleotide treatment for MAST3-associated epilepsy - Prof. David Keays, Sensory and Developmental Neuroscience

Avian Cerebral Organoids - Prof. David Keays, Sensory and Developmental Neuroscience

Identification and Characterisation of Novel Microtubule Associated Proteins - Prof. David Keays, Sensory and Developmental Neuroscience

Transcriptional networks shaping the legume root symbiosis with nitrogen-fixing rhizobia - Prof. Martin Parniske, Plant Genetics

Harnessing natural genetic resources to defend fruits against insect attack - Prof. Martin Parniske, Plant Genetics

For full project descriptions, please visit: https://www.bio.lmu.de/lsm/en/become-an-lsm-student/recruiting-labs-doctoral-positions/index.html#st_accordion__master_2
Master's degree (MSc) or equivalent in biology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, biophysics, biotechnology, medicine, or a related discipline
In exceptional cases, a 4-year Bachelor's degree with Honours (min. 240 ECTS, with written thesis) is accepted
Proficiency in written and spoken English
The most recent final examination must have taken place no more than four years prior to the date of application
There are no tuition fees

An international, multidisciplinary doctoral programme at a world-class research institution
Individual mentoring and a structured Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC)
A wide range of transferable skills workshops, seminars, and career development opportunities
Financial support for conferences and scientific events
A vibrant student community at the LMU Biocenter

jobs.occupation: Testing Operator - Space Hardware Testing (all genders) (Werkstoffprüfer/in (mit Schwerpunkten))
jobs.description:
YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES THE WHY We build pressure vessels and carbon structures for spaceflight. Before our hardware flies, it gets tested — and you keep the testing running. Without you, the test bench stands still. THE WHAT You prepare tests, help run them, and document the results. You work in the lab and at the test bench — hands-on, in a team, with real space hardware every day. Your tasks in detail:
• Prepare and post-process the testing areas: You set up test benches and specimens, tear down after tests, and keep the testing area ready for action. → High Performance: The test bench is ready when the team needs it.
• Run and document tests: You support destructive testing and acceptance testing (NDT) and record every step cleanly. → Accountability: What was tested is documented. No gaps.
• Say what you see: Anything unusual about a specimen, the test bench, or a result — you report it right away, not when someone asks. → Candor: You raise problems before they grow.
• Support the team and infrastructure: You pitch in where needed — in the testing team and with technical infrastructure on site. → Togetherness: We win as a team.
• Learn new things: NDT methods, new test procedures, new materials — you want to grow. We'll train you. → Playfulness: Curiosity is a strength here, not a distraction.

YOUR PROFILE
• Training: Completed vocational training as a materials tester / Werkstoffprüfer (plastics, metals, or fiber composites/CFRP) or comparable technical training.
• Experience: First experience in a test lab or materials testing is a plus — not a must. What matters more: you want to learn.
• Work style: Motivated, reliable, hands-on. You want the job done — and done right.
• Team player: You enjoy working with others and help out when things get busy.
• Languages: German and English, each at B2 minimum — one of the two confident for daily work.
• On-site: This role is 100% on-site in Taufkirchen. The lab and test bench don't fit in a home office.

#LI-Onsite

WHAT WE OFFER
• Creative freedom & responsibility: Autonomy, scope for decision-making and short implementation paths.
• Flexible working hours & remote option: You can work remotely by arrangement.
• Culinary variety: Lunch together with fresh, varied dishes every day.
• Attractive additional benefits: Choose between Deutschlandticket, EGYM-Well pass or a monthly top-up payment card (GivveCard).
• Knowledge exchange at the highest level: Work with experienced engineers and experts from the aerospace industry.
• Dynamic environment: Exciting projects, development opportunities and a start-up atmosphere with agile, cross-functional collaboration.
• Community & team spirit: Monthly blackout events for socialising, networking and exchange.
• Unique working atmosphere : Enjoy the end of the working day on our large roof terrace with a view of the Alps!

About us Blackwave designs, manufactures and ships flight-qualified, commercial off-the-shelf composite overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) for launch vehicles and satellites. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Munich, Germany, the company delivers COPVs from a standardized portfolio with flight heritage. The approach reduces lead time from months to days while ensuring that each tank is qualified and flight-ready. Blackwave's mission is to end COPV failure in spaceflight. The company employs more than 150 people across manufacturing facilities in Germany and Texas.More information at Blackwave.com and the procurement platform COPV.com.

We help people pipette light. Our optoWELL is a programmable LED illumination platform for 24- and 96-well plates, used by labs worldwide in optogenetics, photopharmacology and photodynamic therapy. We are a small team in Freiburg and sell directly to scientists around the globe. To grow, we need one more person who wants to leave the bench and create a lasting role in our startup with us.

What you will own

- Finding researchers who work with light
- Turning them into qualified leads
- Reaching out, following up, and handing warm conversations over to our CEO
- Keeping the pipeline clean and reporting on it
- A smaller share of routine sales admin (quotes, order confirmations, invoices)

You will not be an assistant. You get a clearly defined area, your own numbers, a documented process to start from – and the freedom to improve it.

What you bring

- Some background in light-based research – or the curiosity to dive into it with us; it is a small, friendly field and we will show you around
- A Master's degree or PhD in biology, biochemistry, biotechnology, pharmacy, chemistry or a related field – you can read a paper and pull out what matters
- Excellent written English; German is helpful for day-to-day work but not required
- You enjoy writing short, personal messages and are not discouraged by the fact that most people don't reply
- Structured, self-reliant work over weeks with a weekly check-in rather than daily supervision; solid Excel skills
- Nice to have: experience with CRM tools or AI-assisted literature work

What we offer

- A proven, documented sales process that already works – you copy it first, then improve it and make it your own if you can
- A role built around one measurable outcome – conversations booked with qualified scientists – rather than a to-do list
- Direct work with the founder, short decision paths, real insight into how a scientific instrument is sold worldwide
- Flexible hours, remote days possible after onboarding, office at the Freiburg Innovation Center (FRIZ)
- €42,000–50,000 gross per year at full-time equivalent, depending on experience – i.e. €21,000–25,000 for the 50 % start; the same rate applies if the role grows to full-time

What we are really looking for

Someone who is curious about other people's science and would rather understand a lab's actual problem than pitch a product. Someone who works on their own steam, says so when something is not working, and treats scientists and colleagues with the same respect. If that sounds like you, this is not a side role – it is a seat at the core of a small team.

How this works

You will work directly with me, Kathrin – co-founder, CEO, and so far the one doing this job. Send me an email with your CV and two or three sentences on why you want to leave the bench (no cover letter please, and no multi-page AI slop): k.brenker@optobiolabs.com. Then it is simple: a short conversation, a paid two- to three-hour trial task so we both see what the job actually feels like, and fast feedback – you will hear from me within a week, either way.
